data: Out on a Quest: Writing a Research Essay

Researchers are questers asking research questions to better understand the worldly wilderness we inhabit. They track and read sources, reflect on ideas, form alliances, combat misreading - wielding reading skills and writing implements. They return transformed by the quest, to tell their tale with a well written research essay that adds to how we know the world. This upper-level writing course for literature students will advance the skills learned in WOC and LAA. The drafting process will include basic archival research to find sources for a topic of one’s choice; distinguishing between different kinds of sources; asking research questions; making claims supported by evidence; sustaining an argument; getting and giving revision feedback; and, learning citation systems in addition to MLA. Motivated by the guiding principles of asking questions that perhaps stay unanswered in the process of knowledge creation, this writing intensive course aims to introduce students to the work of research as it gets bigger in scale and complexity. To meet the final goal of writing a proofed and polished 2,500 words research essay by the end of the term, students will complete shorter, targeted tasks for the new skills they are learning. For instance, if they have been introduced to an online archive, or have found one on their own, they may submit a description of it. Other exercises may include annotating a text, creating a glossary of conceptual terms, close-reading, writing summaries of sources they will work with, giving peer feedback, interspersed with revising and submitting drafts at incremental word limits.
